# Basins of a determined law

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`basins-of-a-determined-law` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](basins-of-a-determined-law.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Under any determined law, courses meeting is an equivalence whose classes are basins; a course reaches every returning configuration of its basin, so within finitely many configurations each basin holds one cycle, entered before as many steps as there are configurations.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Within m listed configurations every course enters what returns before step m. (`Becoming.Law.enters_returning_within`)
2. The courses of two configurations meet where at some steps they are at one configuration; after meeting they run together, and meeting is reflexive, symmetric and transitive under any determined law. (`Becoming.Law.Meet`, `Becoming.Law.Meet.refl`, `Becoming.Law.Meet.symm`, `Becoming.Law.Meet.later`, `Becoming.Law.Meet.trans`)
3. A course reaches every returning configuration of its basin; within finitely many configurations each basin holds one cycle. (`Becoming.Law.Meet.reaches_returning`, `Becoming.Law.basin_one_cycle`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; a determined law; finitely many configurations listed where stated.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- How many basins an actual law has.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
